subject: AI
one_line_core_task: Formalise the hardworking-student story in FOL, convert to CNF and prove by resolution that Alice graduates.
question_text: Consider the following story of the "hardworking student": "Anyone who writes the thesis and passes the viva graduates. But anyone who is hardworking or has a guide writes the thesis. If someone has a guide they get support. Anyone who gets support passes the viva. Alice is not hardworking but she has a guide. Prove using resolution that Alice graduates." (6 Marks)
required_keywords: FOL: Forall X (write(X,thesis) AND pass(X,viva) => graduate(X)); Forall X (hardworking(X) OR guide(X) => write(X,thesis)); Forall X (guide(X) => support(X)); Forall X (support(X) => pass(X,viva)); not hardworking(alice) AND guide(alice); negated goal not graduate(alice); clauses C1, C2a, C2b, C3, C4, C5a, C5b, C6; R1 write(alice,thesis); R2 support(alice); R3 pass(alice,viva); R4; R5 not pass(alice,viva); empty clause
key_final_answer: Empty clause derived by refutation, so graduate(alice) is entailed.

subject: AI
one_line_core_task: Use propositional forward and backward chaining to decide whether antibiotics are prescribed for a coughing patient with no fever.
question_text: In a hospital, doctors follow these rules: if a patient has either a fever or a cough, then the patient is considered to have an infection. If a patient has an infection, then antibiotics are prescribed. Additionally, if the patient has a fever, they are also sent for a blood test. Now, suppose a patient has a cough but no fever. Using propositional logic and applying both forward and backward chaining, determine whether the patient will be prescribed antibiotics. (6 Marks)
required_keywords: symbols F, C, I, A, B; rules (F or C) -> I; I -> A; F -> B; facts C true, F false; forward: C gives I gives A; backward: goal A needs I needs F or C, C given; no blood test
key_final_answer: Yes, antibiotics are prescribed (cough implies infection implies antibiotics); no blood test.

one_line_core_task: Compute the joint probability of two office scenarios (E, D, L, W, A) from the given conditional probabilities.
question_text: For the Bayesian network given below: An office is monitored with five binary variables: Employee presence (E): Employees are present 20% of the time. Delivery person (D): Deliveries occur 5% of the time. Lights (L): If employee present -> Lights on 95% of the time. If only delivery person present -> Lights on 80% of the time. If no one present -> Lights on 5% of the time. Window (W): With delivery -> Window breaks 12% of the time. Without delivery -> Window breaks 1% of the time. Alarm (A): Window broken & lights on -> Alarm 99% chance. Window broken & lights off -> Alarm 85% chance. Window intact & lights on -> Alarm 2% chance. Window intact & lights off -> Alarm 0.1% chance. Compute: a) An employee is present, no delivery occurs, lights are on, window intact, and alarm not triggered. What is the probability of this situation? b) No one is present, lights are off, window intact, and alarm not triggered. What is the probability of this situation?
required_keywords: joint probability product P(E)P(D)P(L|E,D)P(W|D)P(A|W,L); a) 0.1751; b) 0.7141
